chunks: Humayd, from Ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

A woman came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) seeking a verdict regarding spending the night in a place other than her own house, while her husband had died. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the people of the Pre-Islamic period, when the husband of a woman died, his wife would mourn for him for twelve months. So when Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), out of mercy for their weakness, He made their waiting period four months and ten (days), and you do not have patience for this?'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling and reasoning for a widow's waiting period (Iddah) regarding staying in her home?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the wisdom behind the four-month-and-ten-day waiting period (Iddah) for widows, framing it as a divine mercy alleviating the harsh twelve-month mourning of the Pre-Islamic era (Jahiliyyah). He notes that while this duration is a concession to women's physical and emotional fragility, it remains a binding obligation, implying that widows should not seek to extend their stay in their late husband's home beyond this prescribed time.

en.hubeali: Humeyd, from Ibn Sama’at, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘A woman who came over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> to seek a verdict regarding the spending of a night in other than her own house, and her husband had died. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In the Pre-Islamic period, when a husband of a woman died, his wife would mourn over him for twelve months. So when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, was Merciful on their weak ones, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Made their waiting period being of four months and ten (days), and you all are not being patient upon this?’
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about the case of a woman whose husband dies and about where she can complete her waiting period.
He (the Imam) said, ‘She can do so wherever she likes but she must not pass a night in a place other than her house.’”
